subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Phoenix and Rebirth
description: A quick, practical guide to The Phoenix and Rebirth.

hook.text: The phoenix burns itself to ash and rises again. No other mythic animal symbolizes resurrection so purely.

buildup.text: Herodotus first described it from Egypt. A bird that lives 500 years, builds a pyre, and is reborn from flame.

discovery.text: Chinese mythology has the fenghuang—often called a phoenix. It represents virtue and the empress's power.

twist.text: Early Christians adopted the phoenix as a symbol of Christ's resurrection. A pagan fire-bird became theology.

climax.text: The phoenix survives because its message is irresistible: destruction is not the end. Something rises from ash.

quiz.question: Who first described the phoenix to the Western world?
